stories.title: The Wolff Playbook
stories.dek: For four years a famous magazine writer coached a convicted sex offender on how to handle reporters, Trump, and his own story. The emails show the coaching in real time.

stories.title: Bannon's Burner
stories.dek: Eighty-nine emails and thousands of text messages between Steve Bannon and Epstein, almost all from 2018: crypto, Europe, "the gunsights," and a documentary that never aired.

stories.title: Mr. Money and the Professor
stories.dek: Larry Summers wrote to Epstein about bitcoin, Trump, Davos, and a woman he was pursuing. The 116 emails ended his board seats in 2025.

stories.title: Watching Donald
stories.dek: Trump is the most discussed third party in the inbox. Across six correspondents, the archive records how Epstein talked about a former friend who became president.

stories.title: Code and Coin
stories.dek: From a 2009 "goal of making money of virtual money" to funding bitcoin's core developers through MIT: a ten-year pursuit, in 276 emails.

stories.title: Island Invitations
stories.dek: Thiel, Hoffman, and the Musk brothers in the inbox: lunches, a $10–20 million fund pitch, a Putin trip nobody took, and the question of "the wildest party on your island."

stories.title: The Black Account
stories.dek: Seventy-three emails to Leon Black, nearly all in 2015, show Epstein running the billionaire's family office from the inside and fighting over his fee.

stories.title: The Barak Channel
stories.dek: Twenty-one emails with Israel's former prime minister: Iran, Syria, Putin, a security startup, and "you should make clear that i dont work for mossad."

stories.title: The Russia File
stories.dek: Putin meetings that were discussed and never documented, a deputy minister's American tour, a $100 million offer for the townhouse, and a wire to Sberbank in the last January.

stories.title: The Gulf Correspondence
stories.dek: A Dubai ports chairman, a former Qatari prime minister, a Sharia-compliant coin, and a palace in Marrakech the lawyers advised against.

stories.title: The Duke's Denial
stories.dek: In four days of emails Prince Andrew asked Epstein to make sure "every statement or legal letter states clearly that I am NOT involved," and Epstein drafted the lines his friend could use.

stories.title: Mandelson's Inbox
stories.dek: Thirty emails with the Labour peer who became Britain's ambassador to Washington, and lost the post in 2025 when they were published.

stories.title: G
stories.dek: Sixty-one emails from 2001 to 2017: Moscow trips, a Clinton Africa itinerary, a Vanity Fair profile, and the morning the allegations went public.

stories.title: The Office
stories.dek: Lesley Groff kept the calendar, Richard Kahn moved the money, Darren Indyke handled the paper. Their emails are the operating system of the archive.

stories.title: The Last Inbox
stories.dek: From the Miami Herald series to the arrest at Teterboro: eight months of settlements, statements, Fed opinions, Flipboard digests, and a list.

stories.title: The Government's Inbox
stories.dek: The DOJ release includes the prosecutors' and agents' own email: the week of the arrest, the Maxwell case, an OPR report, and the 2025 scramble to process the files.

stories.title: Reputation, Inc.
stories.dek: Four months of emails with Al Seckel, who promised that negative articles would "mysteriously disappear from searches," then fought over the bill.

stories.title: The Idea Lab
stories.dek: MIT, Harvard, the Media Lab, and the scientists who kept writing: what the inbox shows about science as social capital.

stories.title: The Islands
stories.dek: A governor's wife on the payroll, a congresswoman in the office, "Trust legislation" from the governor's own address: how the territory ran through the inbox.

stories.title: The Tweet Counter
stories.dek: Through the fall of 2016 a small analytics firm sent Epstein weekly reports on millions of election tweets. It called the result a week early.

stories.title: Flight Operations
stories.dek: Fifty-six emails from the pilot: a Boeing 727 that would not sell, a Gulfstream door, a Cuba form, and three years of flying around a president's Palm Beach weekends.

stories.title: The Reporter
stories.dek: A New York Times financial reporter traded tips, market gossip and Trump stories with Epstein for a decade. The paper later said he should not have.

stories.title: The Dinner Table
stories.dek: Chopra on consciousness, a satirist's atheist prayers, a China commentator's TV series, a film director's Chinese food: the inbox as a salon, 2016–2019.

stories.title: The Casino Man
stories.dek: Nicholas Ribis ran Trump's casinos in the 1990s. From 2016 to the week of the arrest he sent Epstein a running commentary on the man he says he rebuilt.

stories.title: Blue Bubbles
stories.dek: The releases include 104 iMessage logs pulled from device backups. They are shorter, faster and franker than the email, and most of them are with Steve Bannon.

stories.title: The Hot Mic
stories.dek: In April 2015 an ABC News producer told Epstein's lawyers that an on-camera interview with Virginia Roberts was "very likely" to air that week. It did not. Four years later an anchor's hot-mic lament said why, and the inbox shows what the network had been asking.

stories.title: The Deal
stories.dek: The non-prosecution agreement of 2008 is the hinge of the whole story. The DOJ release includes the prosecutors' own emails from the months they wrote it, and from the summer eleven years later when New York decided it did not apply.

stories.title: The Donors
stories.dek: Harvard took his money until 2008 and his visits for a decade after. MIT took both until 2017, as long as the gifts stayed small and unpublicized. The emails show the plumbing: whose money it was, whose name went on it, and who was asked to keep quiet.

stories.title: The Dog That Hasn't Barked
stories.dek: Two emails, eight years apart, that put the future president inside Epstein's own account of his case. Between them, the advice he got on how to use him.

stories.title: Anonymous
stories.dek: Six emails on the mechanics of giving: a draft letter for someone else's $2 million, a "do not contact" list, a bounced $25,000 and a question about the size of the gift.

stories.title: Saturday, July 6
stories.dek: The last day of the inbox, told from both sides of it: the government's script, the jokes with his lawyer, and the Bureau of Prisons emails that followed.

stories.title: What More Does He Want?
stories.dek: Five government emails from the non-prosecution agreement of 2007 and 2008, in the prosecutors' own words, and what happened to the man who signed it.

stories.title: RSVP
stories.dek: The whole Musk correspondence that survives in the releases is short enough to read in a minute. Here it is, with what Musk said about it thirteen years later.

stories.title: The Nobel Chairman
stories.dek: Thorbjørn Jagland ran Norway, then the Council of Europe, then the committee that gives the peace prize. In the inbox he is a correspondent who needs things explained.

stories.title: The Book Club
stories.dek: Drafts, chapters and whole manuscripts moved through the inbox, some of them months before publication. A short history of Epstein as a reader.

stories.title: The Counsel
stories.dek: Kathryn Ruemmler was counsel to President Obama, then a partner at Latham, then the top lawyer at Goldman Sachs. In the inbox she reads the law, and in December 2018 she is on the thread where his response to the Miami Herald is written.

stories.title: Blue Bubbles: Bannon
stories.dek: The recovered iMessage logs are the closest thing in the archive to hearing the two men talk. These four run from the Cohen raid to the week the New York Post called about an underwater office.

stories.title: The Duke's Reply
stories.dek: The week the photograph and the allegations reached the press, in four emails: the forward, the question, the demand and Epstein's draft denial.

stories.title: Ninety Seconds: The Hot Mic
stories.dek: The short cut of The Hot Mic: the request for comment, the advice to ignore the network, and the tape four years later.
